briefs.title: Reliability core: process, locking, state IO

events.wire:
CVM1|A|F
E|Read commit b2866f6 diff in full across all 8 changed files; no scope creep beyond the brief's file list.
E|ProcessRunner.RunAsync: Process.Start wrapped; Win32Exception and Start()==false both return CommandResult{ExitCode=-1,StartFailed=true} instead of throwing. Verified.
E|ProcessRunner timeout: linked CTS with CancelAfter, timeout distinguished from caller cancellation via timeoutCancellation.IsCancellationRequested && !cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested. Kill + bounded DrainAfterKillAsync. Verified.
E|ExecutableLocator.Find: on Windows the extensionless 'exact' probe is now gated behind Path.HasExtension and retried only after the PATHEXT loop, so codex.CMD wins over an extensionless codex shim. Verified by reading the reordered loop.
E|ExclusiveFileLease.AcquireAsync: the original always-true retry filter is gone; bounded by both maximumAttempts and a wall-clock timeout, throwing InvalidOperationException carrying busyMessage and the owner PID. Verified.
E|ExclusiveFileLease exclusivity preserved: share mode moved from None to Read\pDelete, but every acquirer opens FileAccess.ReadWrite, which Read does not permit, so two holders still cannot coexist.
E|StateStore.ReadJsonLineTailAsync opens FileShare.ReadWrite\pFileShare.Delete and seeks the tail rather than File.ReadAllLinesAsync; rotation archive is consulted when the active file is short. Verified.
E|CommandResult.Success redefined as ExitCode == 0 && !TimedOut && !StartFailed, so a timed-out or unlaunchable process cannot be mistaken for success.
E|FknrtdConfig gains AgentTimeoutSeconds=3600 and VerificationTimeoutSeconds=600 as init properties, so a pre-existing config.json without the keys still deserializes and receives defaults.
T|dotnet build FKNRTD.CLI.sln -c Release => Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Run by the auditor in the implementation worktree.
T|dotnet run --project tests/FKNRTD.SelfTest/FKNRTD.SelfTest.csproj -c Release --no-build => 13/13 self-tests passed, exit 0. Run by the auditor, not taken from the report.
T|Self-tests observed to cover the brief's named cases: process timeout, bad executable, bounded lease, concurrent-append tail read, rotation, PATHEXT precedence, legacy config defaults, unlaunchable agent in doctor.
B|UNBOUNDED DRAIN ON NORMAL EXIT PATH (src/FKNRTD.Core/Services/ProcessRunner.cs, RunAsync): after WaitForExitAsync returns normally, 'await Task.WhenAll(stdoutTask, stderrTask)' has no bound and the pumps run on pumpCancellation, which is never cancelled on this path. If the launched CLI spawns a grandchild that inherits the stdout/stderr pipe handles (agent CLIs that start a background daemon or MCP server do exactly this), the pipes never reach EOF and RunAsync hangs forever even though the direct child exited and the configured timeout has elapsed. The timeout only guards WaitForExitAsync, not the drain. This defeats the brief's central acceptance criterion, 'no unbounded hang'. Fix: bound the post-exit drain the same way DrainAfterKillAsync already does, cancelling pumpCancellation and returning what was captured, and mark the result so the caller can tell a truncated capture from a complete one.
B|MINOR (same file): the timeout path returns ExitCode -1, which is indistinguishable from the StartFailed result's -1 in logs. The TimedOut/StartFailed flags disambiguate in code, but any surface that prints only the exit code cannot. Consider distinct sentinels or always printing the flag.
Q|DrainAfterKillAsync's 5s KillDrainTimeout is not configurable; acceptable for now, but if a verification command legitimately produces a large trailing burst the tail may be truncated. Not blocking.

CVM1|A|P
E|Read commit c724a96 diff in full. Scope limited to ProcessRunner.cs, Models.cs and the self-test, as the repair required.
E|The R1 finding is fixed at the right place: the post-exit 'await Task.WhenAll(stdoutTask, stderrTask)' now runs inside the try block under .WaitAsync(waitCancellation), so it shares the run's timeout budget instead of being unbounded.
E|A processExited flag distinguishes a hung child from a hung drain: when the child already exited, CancelAndDrainPumpsAsync cancels the pumps and bounds the wait by KillDrainTimeout instead of pointlessly waiting on an already-dead process, and the error text says 'output drain timed out' rather than the misleading 'process timed out'.
E|CancelAndDrainPumpsAsync is itself bounded: it cancels pumpCancellation first, then awaits WhenAll under .WaitAsync(KillDrainTimeout), swallowing only OperationCanceledException/TimeoutException. No path through it can wait forever.
E|CommandResult.OutputTruncated was added so a caller can distinguish a complete capture from a truncated one. As a side benefit the pre-existing silent truncation at CaptureLimitCharacters is now reported too: OutputCapture.Truncated is set both when a line is clipped and when the cap is already reached.
E|The regression test is a real reproduction, not a stub: fake-agent 'spawn-pipe-holder' starts a grandchild ('hold-pipes') that inherits the stdout/stderr handles and then exits, which is precisely the inherited-pipe scenario from the R1 finding.
E|The test asserts the bound holds (Duration < 2s against a 300ms timeout), that TimedOut and OutputTruncated are both set, that Success is false, and that partial output captured before the parent exited is still returned.
T|dotnet build FKNRTD.CLI.sln -c Release => Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Run by the auditor in the implementation worktree.
T|dotnet run --project tests/FKNRTD.SelfTest/FKNRTD.SelfTest.csproj -c Release --no-build => 14/14 self-tests passed, exit 0. Run by the auditor, not taken from the report.
T|New test 'Post-exit output drain is bounded' observed passing; it is the one that would hang before this commit.
Q|Accepted trade-off: the drain shares the single per-run timeout budget rather than getting its own, so a process that exits just before the deadline gets very little drain time and reports TimedOut with a truncated tail instead of its real exit code. This is defensible as a total wall-clock budget and is now observable via OutputTruncated, but if trailing output loss shows up in practice the drain should get its own smaller independent deadline.
Q|The R1 minor note about ExitCode -1 being shared between the timeout and start-failure paths was not addressed. It is not blocking: TimedOut and StartFailed disambiguate in code, and both paths now carry explanatory text in StandardError.

briefs.title: Workflow correctness: verdict, base refs, git paths

events.wire:
CVM1|A|P
E|Read the full working-tree diff before committing it (8 modified files plus one new AssemblyInfo.cs). Scope matches the brief's file list.
E|Audit verdict: RunAuditStageAsync now calls IsPassingAuditVerdict(report, prompt, success, failure), which first removes the prompt echo via RemovePromptEcho and only then counts markers. A CLI that repeats its prompt can no longer contribute the prompt's own PASS and FAIL lines to the count.
E|Checked the failure direction deliberately: if only part of the prompt is echoed, removal does not match, both markers survive, and IsPassingAuditVerdict returns false. Ambiguity therefore fails closed, which is the brief's requirement that an ambiguous verdict is never a pass.
E|Marker matching is now a regex allowing blockquote, list-bullet, emphasis and trailing-punctuation wrapping while still anchoring the marker to its own line, so a marker mentioned mid-sentence is not counted.
E|Base refs: RepairTaskBaseRefAsync runs at both RunAsync and LandAsync entry, replacing an empty or literal 'HEAD' BaseRef with a resolved local branch and persisting it. ResolveBaseBranchAsync now throws an explicit detached-HEAD error rather than silently returning 'HEAD'.
E|Git paths: GitAsync prepends -c core.quotePath=false to every invocation, and status/diff path listings use -z with NUL-terminated parsing. Both halves of the requirement are met; -z alone already suppresses quoting, so the two are belt and braces rather than redundant.
E|The now-unnecessary backslash-to-forward-slash rewrite was removed from GetDiffPathsAsync, which is correct because -z output already uses forward slashes.
E|EnsureCommittedAsync queries user.name and user.email and throws a message naming both before attempting the commit.
E|Worktree cleanup removes the worktree, runs git worktree prune, and deletes the landed branch.
E|Scope note, accepted: src/FKNRTD.Core/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs adds InternalsVisibleTo("FKNRTD.SelfTest"). That line was listed under a later brief, but it is required here for the self-tests to reach the internal IsPassingAuditVerdict, so it is justified in place rather than scope creep.
T|dotnet build FKNRTD.CLI.sln -c Release => Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Run by the auditor in the implementation worktree.
T|dotnet run --project tests/FKNRTD.SelfTest/FKNRTD.SelfTest.csproj -c Release --no-build => 16/16 self-tests passed, exit 0. Run by the auditor, not taken from the report.
T|Two new named tests observed passing: 'Audit verdict ignores echoed prompt' and 'Git paths round trip verbatim'.
T|All 14 previously landed tests still pass, so the reliability work from brief #1 did not regress.
Q|RemovePromptEcho removes only an exact normalized substring match of the whole prompt. A partial or reformatted echo is not removed. This cannot cause a false PASS (the surviving FAIL marker forces failure) but can cause a false FAIL on an otherwise passing audit. Acceptable for revision 1 because it errs toward refusing to land.
Q|The implementing seat could not commit its own work: Codex's workspace-write sandbox denies writes to the linked worktree's Git metadata under the main repository's .git/worktrees/. The auditing seat committed the working tree unchanged and recorded why in the commit message. The ghostrider runtime has since been fixed to pass --add-dir for the main .git directory, so later rounds should self-commit.

briefs.title: Renderer correctness: display width, layout, frame tests

events.wire:
CVM1|A|P
E|Read the full working-tree diff before committing it: Canvas.cs, DashboardApp.cs, CommandDispatcher.cs, the self-test project file and Program.cs, plus a new src/FKNRTD.Cli/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs. Scope matches the brief.
E|Canvas.Text.DisplayWidth measures by grapheme cluster via StringInfo.GetTextElementEnumerator, taking the max rune width per cluster and treating a cluster carrying U+FE0F or U+20E3 as at least two columns. That is the correct shape: combining marks contribute zero and do not split, and emoji presentation is not undercounted.
E|InternalsVisibleTo was added to the Cli assembly in its own Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs, matching the pattern brief #2 established for Core. Dashboard internals were not made public.
E|INDEPENDENT RENDER VERIFICATION, not a re-run of the implementer's tests: rendered real frames from the built binary with 'dashboard -once -no-color' at widths 60, 72, 84, 100, 119, 120, 140 and 200, and measured every line with a separate Unicode width implementation (Python unicodedata east_asian_width plus combining). Every line matched the requested width exactly at every width; zero lines off.
E|Zero ESC (U+001B) characters appeared in any -no-color frame, confirming the colour-free contract from the outside rather than from the renderer's own code path.
E|CJK and emoji regression checked against the real binary: created tasks titled with Japanese text and an emoji, confirmed wide characters are actually present in the rendered frames, and confirmed every line still measured exactly the requested width at 84, 120 and 160. This is the original defect and it is fixed.
E|Joined borders confirmed by inspection of a rendered 120-column frame: junctions use the correct characters and a grep for doubled corner seams returns zero occurrences.
E|CJK task titles truncate with an ellipsis at the panel boundary without shifting the frame.
E|The -width and -height overrides work on the real binary and are what made the independent measurement possible.
T|dotnet build FKNRTD.CLI.sln -c Release => Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Run by the auditor in the implementation worktree.
T|dotnet run --project tests/FKNRTD.SelfTest/FKNRTD.SelfTest.csproj -c Release --no-build => 18/18 self-tests passed, exit 0. Run by the auditor.
T|Two new named tests observed passing: 'Dashboard frames preserve display width and topology' and 'Dashboard CLI dimensions override detection'.
T|All 16 previously landed tests still pass, so briefs #1 and #2 did not regress.
T|External frame measurement across 8 widths plus 3 CJK widths, described above, performed by the auditor with an independent width implementation.
Q|Display width is inherently terminal-dependent. The implementation follows East Asian Wide/Fullwidth plus emoji presentation, which matches Windows Terminal and most modern emulators, but a terminal that renders ambiguous-width characters as double will still disagree. That is a property of the problem, not a defect in this change.
Q|The implementing seat could not commit: its sandbox sets an explicit Write deny on the Git common-dir, so index.lock could not be created in the linked worktree. On Windows an explicit deny overrides the --add-dir allow added to ghostrider earlier, so that mitigation is insufficient for codex specifically. Codex reported the blocker honestly rather than leaving the work unexplained. The auditing seat committed the working tree unchanged.
